title: First lessons: price, setup and Bechet's enthusiasm
summary: Wilber was the school's only student at $5 a lesson; Bechet was keen to teach his idea of improvisation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And so I, I came over and, and, uh, bought my clarinet and played for him. And I guess he, he was really pleased at the start because I obviously was trying to play like he, you know, he was my idol.
What kind of clarinet did you have in those days?

By then I'd graduated to a wooden clarinet, uh, BAME. I don't remember what make it was. Yeah. So, uh, then I started taking lessons once a week from him. And it was, they were supposed to be our lessons, but they always lasted much longer. Yeah.
How much did he charge for the way?
I think it was $5 a lesson. That's a pretty good price.
And he got, he got very interested and excited about teaching. I was the only student in the school. I mean. Oh really? Yeah. You mean he didn't? That was all I was.
Yet he was trying to make a go of it, huh? Well, he never had a really kind of realistic picture of it, you know.
No, I guess not. No, he shouldn't.
But, uh, he was very interested in, in trying to teach somebody his idea of improvisation, you know.
